title.zh: 卷四百〇八 列傳第一百六十七 吳昌裔 汪綱 陳宓 王霆
title.en: Volume 408 Biographies 167: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting
title.raw: 卷四百〇八 列傳第一百六十七 吳昌裔 汪綱 陳宓 王霆 Volume 408 Biographies 167: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting

sentences.zh: 吳昌裔汪綱陳宓王霆

translations.literal: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, and Wang Ting

sentences.zh: 吳昌裔，字季永，中江人。

translations.literal: Wu Changyi, styled Jiyong, was a man of Zhongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changyi, styled Jiyong, was a native of Zhongjiang.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，與兄泳痛自植立，不肯逐時好，得程頤、張載、朱熹諸書，輒研繹不倦。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, with his elder brother Yong he painfully established himself on his own, unwilling to follow the fashions of the age; whenever he obtained the books of Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Zhu Xi, and others, he would study and interpret them without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he and his elder brother Yong rigorously made their own way in the world, refusing to follow prevailing fashions. Whenever he obtained works by Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Zhu Xi, and others, he would study and interpret them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年舉進士，聞漢陽守黃幹得熹之學，往從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination; hearing that Huang Gan, prefect of Hanyang, had obtained Xi's learning, he went to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiading reign (1214) he passed the jinshi examination. Hearing that Huang Gan, prefect of Hanyang, had inherited Zhu Xi's teaching, he went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 調閩中尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as assistant in the Minzhong guard office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant in the Minzhong guard office.

sentences.zh: 利路轉運使曹彥約聞其賢，俾司糴場。

translations.literal: Cao Yanyue, transport commissioner of the Lili circuit, hearing of his worth, had him oversee the grain-purchase stations.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue, transport commissioner of the Lili circuit, heard of his ability and put him in charge of the grain-purchase stations.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，議糴上流，昌裔請發本倉所儲數萬而徐糴以償，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the year was famine; it was proposed to purchase grain upstream; Changyi requested that several tens of thousands stored in the local granary be released first and grain gradually purchased to repay; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: There was a famine that year. When officials proposed buying grain upstream, Changyi asked that tens of thousands of piculs stored in the local granary be released first and gradually repurchased to make restitution. His plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 調眉州教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be instructor at Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as instructor at Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 眉士故尚蘇軾學，昌裔取諸經為之講說，祠周惇頤及顥、頤、載、熹，揭《白鹿洞學規》，仿潭州釋奠儀，簿正祭器，士習丕變。

translations.literal: The scholars of Meizhou had long esteemed Su Shi's learning; Changyi took the classics to lecture for them, set up shrines to Zhou Dunyi and Hao, Yi, Zai, and Xi, posted the Regulations of the White Deer Grotto Academy, imitated the Tanzhou libation ceremony, put the ritual vessels in proper order on the register, and scholarly practice was greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars of Meizhou had long favored Su Shi's school of learning. Changyi lectured on the classics instead, erected shrines to Zhou Dunyi and to Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, posted the White Deer Grotto Academy regulations, imitated the Tanzhou libation ceremony, put the ritual vessels in proper order on the register, and scholarly practice was thoroughly transformed.

sentences.zh: 製置使崔與之薦之，改知華陽縣。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Cui Yuzhi recommended him; he was changed to magistrate of Huayang County.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Cui Yuzhi recommended him, and he was appointed magistrate of Huayang County.

sentences.zh: 修學宮，來四方士，斥羨錢二十萬緡，買良田備旱。

translations.literal: He repaired the school palace, drew scholars from the four directions, expended two hundred thousand strings of surplus funds, and bought fertile fields to guard against drought.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the county school, attracted scholars from all quarters, spent two hundred thousand strings of surplus funds, and purchased fertile fields as a reserve against drought.

sentences.zh: 通判眉州，著《苦言》十篇，慮蜀甚悉。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Meizhou, he composed ten chapters of Bitter Words, with very thorough concern for Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Meizhou, he wrote ten chapters of Bitter Words, expressing very thorough concern for the security of Shu.

sentences.zh: 攝郡事，禦軍有紀律。

translations.literal: Acting in prefectural affairs, he kept the army under discipline.
translations.idiomatic: While acting prefect, he kept the troops under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 尋權漢州，故事比攝官，奉饋皆如真，昌裔命削其半。

translations.literal: Soon he held Hanzhou in temporary authority; by precedent compared with acting officials, stipends and gifts were all as for the real post; Changyi ordered them cut in half.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as acting prefect of Hanzhou. By precedent, acting officials received stipends and gifts equal to those of regular appointees; Changyi ordered these cut in half.

sentences.zh: 核兵籍，興社倉，郡政畢舉。

translations.literal: He verified the military registers, established community granaries, and prefectural administration was fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the military registers, established community granaries, and brought prefectural administration fully up to standard.

sentences.zh: 興元帥趙彥呐議東納武仙，西結秦、鞏，人莫敢言，昌裔獨奮筆力辨其非。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan'a, military commissioner of Xingyuan, proposed accepting Wuxian in the east and allying with Qin and Gong in the west; no one dared speak; Changyi alone took up his brush and vigorously argued the error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan'a, military commissioner of Xingyuan, proposed accepting the Jin general Wuxian in the east and allying with Qin and Gong in the west. No one else dared object, but Changyi alone took up his brush and argued forcefully that the plan was wrong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，武仙敗，二州之民果叛。

translations.literal: Before long Wuxian was defeated, and the people of the two prefectures indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wuxian was defeated, and the people of the two prefectures did in fact revolt.

sentences.zh: 台臣故事，季詣獄點檢。

translations.literal: By censorial precedent, each season one went to the prison to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: By censorial precedent, each season the censor went to the prison to inspect the inmates.

sentences.zh: 時有爭常州田萬四千畝，平江亦數百畝，株逮百餘人，視其牘，乃趙善湘之子汝櫄、汝榟也，州縣不敢決，昌裔連疏劾罷之。

translations.literal: At the time there was dispute over fourteen thousand mu of fields in Changzhou and several hundred mu in Pingjiang; over a hundred persons were implicated; viewing the documents, they were the sons of Zhao Shanxiang, Ruchao and Ruzi; prefecture and county dared not decide; Changyi submitted successive memorials impeaching and removing them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a dispute arose over fourteen thousand mu of land in Changzhou and several hundred mu in Pingjiang, implicating more than a hundred people. When he examined the documents, he found that the claimants were Zhao Shanxiang's sons Ruchao and Ruzi. The prefecture and county dared not decide the case, so Changyi submitted successive memorials impeaching them until they were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 冬洊雷，春大雨雪，昌裔居齋宮秉燭草疏，凡上躬缺失，宮庭嬖私，廟堂除授，皆以為言。

translations.literal: In winter thunder came repeatedly; in spring great rain and snow fell; Changyi dwelt in the fasting palace, holding a candle to draft memorials; whatever concerned the sovereign's person, omissions, palace favorites and private interests, and court appointments—all were spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated thunder sounded in winter, and heavy rain and snow fell in spring. Changyi stayed in the fasting palace, drafting memorials by candlelight. He spoke on every matter touching the emperor's own conduct, palace favorites and private interests, and court appointments.

sentences.zh: 又言：“將帥方命，女寵私謁，舊黨之用，邊疆之禍，皆此陰類。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Generals defying orders, female favorites' private audiences, employment of old faction members, frontier calamities—all are of this yin sort."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Generals who defy orders, private audiences granted to imperial consorts, the reuse of old faction members, and frontier disasters—all stem from this class of hidden influence."

sentences.zh: 且曰：“今大昕坐朝，間有時不視事之文；

translations.literal: And he said: "Now at dawn the emperor sits at court, yet occasionally there are documents of not attending to affairs;"
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Nowadays the emperor holds court at dawn, yet from time to time there appear notices that he is not attending to affairs;"

sentences.zh: 私第謁假，或有時不入堂之報。

translations.literal: "from his private residence requests for leave, or sometimes reports of not entering the hall."
translations.idiomatic: "from his private residence come requests for leave, and sometimes reports that he has not entered the audience hall."

sentences.zh: 上有耽樂慆逸之漸，下無協恭和衷之風。

translations.literal: Above there is the beginning of indulgence in pleasure and dissipation; below there is no wind of united respect and harmony of heart.
translations.idiomatic: Above, there are signs that the emperor is slipping into indulgence and idleness; below, there is no spirit of united respect and harmony among officials.

sentences.zh: 內則嬖禦懷私，為君心之蠹；

translations.literal: Within, favored attendants harbor private aims and are worms in the ruler's heart;
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, favored attendants pursue private ends and eat away at the ruler's judgment;

sentences.zh: 外則子弟寡謹，為朝政之累。

translations.literal: without, sons and younger kin lack caution and are a burden on court administration.
translations.idiomatic: outside it, the emperor's sons and younger kinsmen lack restraint and burden court administration.

sentences.zh: 遊言噂遝，寵賂章聞，欲《簫》、《勺》大和，得乎？”

translations.literal: Loose talk and slander swarm; favor and bribes are openly heard of—can one wish for the great harmony of the Xiao and Shao?
translations.idiomatic: Loose talk and slander abound, and favor and bribes are openly reported. How can one expect the great harmony of the Xiao and Shao music?

sentences.zh: 又念蜀事阽危，條四事以進：實規橅，審功賞，訪軍實，儲帥才。

translations.literal: He also considered that affairs in Shu were on the brink of peril and listed four matters to present: solidify planning, examine merit and rewards, investigate military realities, and store up commanders' talent.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that affairs in Shu were on the brink of collapse, he submitted four proposals: put planning on a solid footing, scrutinize rewards for merit, investigate the true state of the army, and cultivate a reserve of commanders.

sentences.zh: 時有果、閬州守臣逃遁而進職，有知遂寧李煒父子足跡不至邊庭而受賞，僨軍之趙楷、棄城之朱揚祖皆不加罰；

translations.literal: At the time there were prefects of Guo and Langzhou who fled yet were promoted in rank; Li Wei, prefect of Suining, and his son, whose footsteps never reached the frontier, yet received rewards; Zhao Kai, who stirred the army to mutiny, and Zhu Yangzu, who abandoned the city—all went unpunished;
translations.idiomatic: At the time prefects of Guo and Langzhou who had fled were promoted in rank. Li Wei, prefect of Suining, and his son received rewards though their footsteps never reached the frontier. Zhao Kai, who had incited mutiny in the army, and Zhu Yangzu, who had abandoned his city, were not punished at all;

sentences.zh: 又帥臣趙彥呐年老智衰，其子淫刑黷貨，士卒不用命，安癸仲恥遭抨彈，經營復用，欲起謫籍以代帥垣，昌裔皆抗疏彈擊。

translations.literal: further, the commander Zhao Yan'a was old and his wisdom declined; his son practiced licentious punishments and greedy seizure of goods; soldiers did not obey orders; An Guizhong, shamed at being impeached, maneuvered for reuse and wished to raise men from the banishment rolls to replace the commandery—Changyi in every case submitted defiant memorials to impeach and attack.
translations.idiomatic: and military commissioner Zhao Yan'a was old and failing in judgment, while his son inflicted cruel punishments and took bribes and the troops would not obey orders. An Guizhong, shamed at being impeached, maneuvered for reinstatement and sought to recall men from the banishment rolls to replace the frontier command—Changyi submitted forceful memorials attacking each of these abuses.

sentences.zh: 又曆言三邊之事曰：“今朝廷之上，百辟晏然，言論多於施行，浮文妨於實務。

translations.literal: He also spoke in sequence on the three frontiers, saying: "Now above the court the hundred officials are at ease; talk exceeds execution; floating documents obstruct practical affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length on affairs along the three frontiers: "At court today the hundred officials are at ease. Talk outruns action, and empty paperwork obstructs real work."

sentences.zh: 後族王宮之冗費，列曹坐局之常程，群工閑慢之差除，諸道非泛之申請，以至土木經營，時節宴遊，神霄祈禳，大禮錫賚，藻飾治具，無異平時。

translations.literal: The redundant expenses of empresses' kin and princely palaces, the routine procedures of the various bureaus sitting at their desks, the leisurely removals of the mass of officials, the non-routine applications from the circuits, down to construction in earth and wood, seasonal banquets and excursions, Shenxiao prayers and exorcisms, great ritual bestowals, and ornamented administrative arrangements—none differed from normal times.
translations.idiomatic: Redundant spending on empresses' kin and princely palaces, the routine paperwork of the various bureaus, leisurely transfers among officials, non-routine petitions from the circuits, construction projects, seasonal banquets and excursions, Shenxiao prayers and exorcisms, great ritual gifts and grants, and ornamental displays of good government—all continued as in normal times.

sentences.zh: 至於治兵足食之方，脩車備馬之事，乃缺略不講。”

translations.literal: As for methods of governing troops and securing provisions, and matters of repairing chariots and preparing horses—they were omitted and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet methods for training troops and securing provisions, and for repairing chariots and preparing horses, were neglected entirely.

sentences.zh: 且援靖康之敝，痛哭言之。

translations.literal: He also cited the abuses of the Jingkang era and spoke with bitter weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the disasters of the Jingkang era and spoke through tears.

sentences.zh: 出為大理少卿，屢疏引去，不許。

translations.literal: He went out as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; repeatedly in memorials he sought withdrawal; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He repeatedly memorialized asking to resign, but was not permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 會杜範再入台，擊參政李鳴復，謂昌裔與範善，必相為謀者，數讒之，以權工部侍郎出參讚四川宣撫司軍事。

translations.literal: When Du Fan again entered the Censorate and attacked Vice Grand Councilor Li Mingfu, it was said that Changyi and Fan were on good terms and must be plotting together; he was slandered repeatedly and, as Acting Vice Minister of Works, was sent out to participate in and assist the military affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fan reentered the Censorate and attacked Vice Grand Councilor Li Mingfu, opponents said that Changyi and Fan were close and must be acting in concert. Changyi was slandered repeatedly and, as Acting Vice Minister of Works, was sent out to assist the military affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 人曰：“此李綱救太原也。

translations.literal: People said: "This is Li Gang saving Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: People said, "This is like Li Gang being sent to save Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 太原不可救，特以綱主戰，故出之耳。”

translations.literal: Taiyuan could not be saved; it was only because Gang favored war that he was sent out.
translations.idiomatic: "Taiyuan could not be saved; Li Gang was sent out only because he favored war."

sentences.zh: 昌裔曰：“君命也，不可不亟行。”

translations.literal: Changyi said: "It is the ruler's command; one must go at once."
translations.idiomatic: Changyi replied, "It is the ruler's command. I must set out at once."

sentences.zh: 慷慨襆被出關，忽得疾，中道病甚，帝聞之，授秘閣修撰，改嘉興府。

translations.literal: With generous spirit he wrapped his bedding and left the pass; suddenly he fell ill; on the road his illness grew severe; the emperor heard of it and appointed him Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion, changing him to Jiaxing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He wrapped his bedding with high resolve and set out through the pass. Suddenly he fell ill, and on the road his condition grew grave. When the emperor heard of it, he appointed him Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion and transferred him to Jiaxing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昌裔曰：“吾以疾不能歸救父母，上負聖恩，下負此心，若舍遠就近，舍危就安，人其謂我何？”

translations.literal: Changyi said: "Because of illness I cannot return to rescue my parents; above I fail the sage grace; below I fail this heart—if I abandon the distant for the near, abandon peril for safety, what will people say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: Changyi said, "Because of illness I cannot go back to save my parents. I fail the emperor above and my own conscience below. If I abandon the distant post for a nearby one, abandon danger for safety, what will people say of me?"

sentences.zh: 辭至四五，而言者以避事論矣。

translations.literal: He declined four or five times, and remonstrators discussed him as avoiding duty.
translations.idiomatic: He declined four or five times, and critics accused him of shirking duty.

sentences.zh: 改贛州，辭，以右文殿修撰主管鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Ganzhou; he declined and, as Right Culture Hall compiler, supervised Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ganzhou, declined the post, and served as Right Culture Hall compiler in charge of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提刑，辭，改知婺州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Eastern Zhejiang judicial intendant; he declined and was changed to prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial intendant of Eastern Zhejiang, declined, and was appointed prefect of Wuzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 婺告旱，民日夜望之，乃不忍終辭，減騶從供帳，遣僚佐召邑令周行阡陌，蠲粟八萬一千石、錢二十五萬緡有奇。

translations.literal: Wuzhou reported drought; the people day and night looked to him; he could not bear to decline to the end; he reduced escorts and provision accounts, sent aides to summon county magistrates to tour the fields, and remitted eighty-one thousand piculs of grain and more than two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou reported drought, and the people looked to him day and night. He could not bring himself to decline the post after all. He reduced his escort and official expenses, sent aides to summon county magistrates to tour the fields, and remitted eighty-one thousand piculs of grain and more than two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 加集英殿修撰，卒，以寶章閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: He was advanced to compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence; he died, and was granted retirement as Baozhang Pavilion attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence. When he died, he was granted retirement with the title of Baozhang Pavilion attendant.

sentences.zh: 昌裔剛正莊重，遇事敢言，典章多所閑習。

translations.literal: Changyi was upright, stern, and dignified; in affairs he dared to speak; he was well versed in many regulations and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi was upright, stern, and dignified, daring to speak out on public affairs, and well versed in regulations and statutes.

sentences.zh: 嚐輯至和、紹興諸臣奏議本末。

translations.literal: He once compiled the origins and outcomes of memorial proposals by various ministers in the Zhihe and Shaoxing eras.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the origins and outcomes of memorial proposals by ministers of the Zhihe and Shaoxing eras.

sentences.zh: 名《儲鑒》。

translations.literal: It was titled Stored Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He titled it Stored Mirror.

sentences.zh: 又會粹周、漢以至宋蜀道得失，興師取財之所，名《蜀鑒》。

translations.literal: He also gathered and distilled the gains and losses of the Shu routes from Zhou and Han down to Song, and the places where armies were raised and wealth taken, naming it Mirror of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the successes and failures along the Shu routes from Zhou and Han down to Song, and the places where armies were raised and wealth extracted, titling the work Mirror of Shu.

sentences.zh: 有奏議、《四書講義》、《鄉約口義》、《諸老記聞》、《容台議禮》、文集行於世。

translations.literal: He had memorial proposals, Lectures on the Meaning of the Four Books, Oral Expositions of the Village Compact, Records Heard from Various Elders, Rites Discussed at the Guest Terrace, and collected writings circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Memorial Proposals, Lectures on the Meaning of the Four Books, Oral Expositions of the Village Compact, Records Heard from Various Elders, Rites Discussed at the Guest Terrace, and collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 初，昌裔與徐清叟、杜範一日並入台，皆天下正士，四方想聞風采，人至和《三諫詩》以侈之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Changyi with Xu Qingsou and Du Fan on a single day all entered the Censorate; all were upright men under heaven; the four directions longed to hear their bearing; people even harmonized the Three Remonstrators Poem to extol them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Changyi had entered the Censorate on the same day as Xu Qingsou and Du Fan. All three were men of integrity known throughout the realm, and people everywhere looked to their example. Some even composed a Three Remonstrators Poem in their praise.

sentences.zh: 然才七閱月以遷，故莫不惋惜雲。

translations.literal: Yet after only seven months he was transferred, so all regret it, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after only seven months he was transferred, and all regretted it deeply.

sentences.zh: 後諡忠肅。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 汪綱，字仲舉，黟縣人，簽書樞密院勃之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Gang, styled Zhongju, was a man of Yixian County, great-grandson of Bo, who had signed documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gang, styled Zhongju, was a native of Yixian County and the great-grandson of Bo, who had held the post of document signer at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以祖任入官，淳熙十四年中銓試，調鎮江府司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's yin privilege he entered office; in the fourteenth year of Chunxi he passed the selection examination and was assigned as revenue recorder of Zhenjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his grandfather's yin privilege. In the fourteenth year of the Chunxi reign (1187) he passed the selection examination and was appointed revenue recorder of Zhenjiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馬大同鎮京口，強毅自任，綱言論獨不詭隨。

translations.literal: Ma Datong garrisoned Jingkou, strong and resolute in his own judgment; Gang alone in speech and discussion did not bend or follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Datong was stationed at Jingkou, he was forceful and self-willed. Gang alone refused to bend his views to please him.

sentences.zh: 議者欲以兩淮鐵錢交子行於沿江，廷議令大同倡率行之，綱貽書曰：“邊麵行鐵錢，慮銅寶泄於外耳。

translations.literal: Discussants wished to circulate the Huai iron cash exchange notes along the river coast; court discussion ordered Datong to take the lead in implementing it; Gang sent a letter saying: "On the frontier they use iron cash because they fear copper treasure leaking abroad."
translations.idiomatic: Some officials proposed circulating the Huai region's iron cash exchange notes along the Yangzi coast. The court ordered Datong to take the lead in implementing the plan. Gang wrote to him: "On the frontier they use iron cash because they fear copper currency leaking abroad."

sentences.zh: 私鑄盛行，故錢輕而物重。

translations.literal: Private casting flourished, so cash was light and goods heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Private coining is widespread, so money is cheap and goods dear.

sentences.zh: 今若場務出納不以鐵錢取息，堅守四色請買舊制，冶鑄定額不求餘羨，重禁以戢私鑄，支散邊戍與在軍中半者無異，不以鐵錢準折，則淮民將自便之，何至以敝內郡邪？”

translations.literal: Now if market stations did not take interest in iron cash on receipts and disbursements, firmly upheld the old system of four-color purchase requests, set smelting quotas without seeking surplus profit, strictly forbade to check private casting, and disbursed to frontier garrisons no differently from those in the army, not converting at iron cash rates—then Huai people would find it convenient themselves; why reach the point of harming inner commanderies?
translations.idiomatic: If market stations no longer took interest in iron cash on receipts and disbursements, if the old four-color purchase system were strictly upheld, if smelting quotas were fixed without seeking surplus profit, if private coining were sternly suppressed, and if payments to frontier garrisons were made no differently than to troops in the interior, without converting at iron-cash rates, the people of the Huai region would find their own remedy. Why harm the inner commanderies?

sentences.zh: 大同始悟。

translations.literal: Datong then understood.
translations.idiomatic: Datong then saw the point.

sentences.zh: 試湖南轉運司，又中，綱笑曰：“此豈足以用世澤物耶？”

translations.literal: He tested at the Hunan transport office and passed again; Gang laughed and said: "How can this suffice to serve the age and benefit things?"
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Hunan transport office examination as well. Gang laughed and said, "How can this be enough to serve the world and benefit the people?"

sentences.zh: 乃刻意問學，博通古今，精究義理；

translations.literal: He then devoted himself to inquiry and learning, broadly penetrating past and present, finely investigating principle and meaning;
translations.idiomatic: He then devoted himself to serious study, mastering past and present and probing principle to its roots;

sentences.zh: 覃思本原。

translations.literal: he pondered deeply the root origin.
translations.idiomatic: and pondered deeply the foundations of learning.

sentences.zh: 調桂陽軍平陽縣令，縣連溪峒，蠻蜒與居，綱一遇以恩信。

translations.literal: He was assigned magistrate of Pingyang County in Guiyang Command; the county bordered stream gorges; Man and Yan peoples dwelt together; Gang at first encounter treated them with grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Pingyang County in Guiyang Command. The county bordered stream gorges where Man and Yan peoples lived. Gang won them over from the first with kindness and good faith.

sentences.zh: 科罰之害既三十年，綱下車，首白諸台，罷之。

translations.literal: The harm of penal levies had already lasted thirty years; when Gang took office, he first reported to the various censorial offices and abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: Penal levies had plagued the county for thirty years. As soon as Gang took office, he reported to the censorial offices and had them abolished.

sentences.zh: 桂陽歲貢銀二萬九千餘兩，而平陽當其三分之二。

translations.literal: Guiyang annually presented more than twenty-nine thousand taels of silver, and Pingyang bore two-thirds of it.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang Command annually presented more than twenty-nine thousand taels of silver, of which Pingyang County was responsible for two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 綱謂向者銀礦坌發價輕，故可勉以應，今地寶已竭，市於他郡，其價倍蓰，願力請痛蠲損之。

translations.literal: Gang said that formerly silver mines had burst forth and prices were low, so one could strain to meet the quota; now the land's treasure was exhausted; buying from other commanderies, the price doubled and more; he wished to petition forcefully for a sharp reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said that formerly silver mines had been abundant and prices low, so the quota could barely be met. Now the local deposits were exhausted and silver had to be bought in other commanderies at more than double the price. He petitioned urgently for a sharp reduction in the quota.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，旁邑有曹伍者，群聚惡少入境，強貸發廩，眾至千餘，挾界頭、牛橋二砦兵為援，地盤踞萬山間，前後令未嚐一涉其境，不虞綱之至也，相率出迎。

translations.literal: In a famine year, in a neighboring county there was a Cao Wu who gathered wicked youths to enter the border, forcibly borrowing and opening granaries; the crowd reached over a thousand; they relied on the soldiers of the Jietou and Niuqiao two forts as support; the land sprawled among ten thousand mountains; magistrates before and after had never once entered its territory; they did not expect Gang's arrival; they came out together to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year, a man named Cao Wu in a neighboring county gathered ruffians to cross the border, forcibly borrowing grain and breaking open granaries. His band numbered more than a thousand and was backed by troops from the Jietou and Niuqiao forts. The region lay among countless mountains, and no previous magistrate had ever ventured there. They did not expect Gang to come, but when he did they came out together to meet him.

sentences.zh: 綱已夙具酒食，令之曰：“汝何敢亂，順者得食，亂者就誅。”

translations.literal: Gang had long since prepared wine and food; he ordered them: "How dare you make disorder—those who submit receive food; those who rebel face execution."
translations.idiomatic: Gang had already prepared wine and food. He ordered them: "How dare you make trouble? Those who submit will be fed; those who resist will be executed."

sentences.zh: 夜宿砦中，呼砦官詰責不能防守狀，皆皇恐伏地請死，杖其首惡者八人，發粟振糶，民賴以安。

translations.literal: He lodged overnight in the fort, summoned the fort officers and rebuked them for inability to defend; all in terror prostrated themselves begging death; he caned the eight chief villains, released grain and sold relief grain, and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He spent the night in the fort, summoned the fort officers, and rebuked them for failing to keep order. They prostrated themselves in terror and begged for death. He caned the eight ringleaders, released grain, and sold relief grain at fair prices, and the people were restored to peace.

sentences.zh: 改知金壇縣，親嫌，更弋陽縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Jintan County; because of kinship taboo, he was moved to Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jintan County, but because of a kinship taboo was transferred to Yiyang County instead.

sentences.zh: 父義和為侍御史主管佑神觀。

translations.literal: His father Yihe was investigating censor in charge of the You Shen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yihe had served as investigating censor in charge of the You Shen Observatory.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父喪，服除，知蘭溪縣，決擿如神。

translations.literal: Soon he mourned his father's death; when mourning ended, he was magistrate of Lanxi County; his judgments and investigations were like a spirit's.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his father's death. When the mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Lanxi County, where his judgments seemed almost uncanny in their accuracy.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，郡倚辦勸分，綱謂勸分所以助義倉，一切行之，非所謂安富恤貧也，願假常平錢為糶本，使得循環迭濟。

translations.literal: In a drought year the prefecture relied on organizing mutual aid; Gang said mutual aid was to assist the charity granaries—carrying it out wholesale was not what is called enriching the secure and relieving the poor; he wished to borrow Ever-Normal granary funds as capital for relief sales so that circulation could aid in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year the prefecture relied on organizing mutual aid among the wealthy. Gang said mutual aid was meant to supplement the charity granaries, and applying it wholesale was not true relief for the poor. He asked to borrow Ever-Normal granary funds as capital for relief sales so that grain could circulate and aid the needy in turn.

sentences.zh: 又躬勸富民浚築塘堰，大興水利，餓者得食其力，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: He also personally urged wealthy households to dredge and build ponds and weirs, greatly promoting waterworks; the hungry obtained food by their labor, and very many were wholly saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: He also personally urged wealthy households to dredge ponds and build weirs, greatly expanding irrigation works. The hungry earned their food by labor, and very many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 郡守張抑及部使者列綱為一道荒政之冠。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked Gang as the crown of famine administration in the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked Gang the foremost in famine relief in the circuit.

sentences.zh: 以言去，邑人相率投軌直其事，綱力止之。

translations.literal: He left because of remonstrance; the people of the district together cast themselves on the carriage tracks to state the facts directly; Gang forcefully stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: He left office after speaking out on policy. The people of the district threw themselves before his carriage to plead his case, but Gang firmly stopped them.

sentences.zh: 繼知太平縣，主管兩浙轉運司文字，未赴，罹內艱，擢監行在左藏西庫。

translations.literal: He next was magistrate of Taiping County and supervisor of documents for the Two-Zhe transport office; before he went, he suffered inner mourning and was promoted to supervise the Western Treasury of the Left Storehouse at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He next served as magistrate of Taiping County and was assigned to handle documents for the Two-Zhe transport office, but before he could take up the latter post he mourned a close relative and was promoted to supervise the Western Treasury of the Left Storehouse at the capital.

sentences.zh: 屬金人殺其主允濟自立，遣使來告襲位，議者即欲遣幣，綱言：‘使名不遜，當止之境上，姑命左帑視例計辦，或且留京口總司，令盱眙諭之曰：‘紀年名節，皆犯先朝避忌，歲幣乃爾前主所增，今既易代，當復隆興、大定之舊。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens killed their ruler Yunji and established themselves, they sent envoys to announce succession to the throne; discussants at once wished to send tribute; Gang said: "The envoy's title is not deferential; he should be stopped at the border; for the moment order the Left Treasury to examine precedent and calculate arrangements, or detain him at the Jingkou general headquarters and have Chuyi instruct him: 'The reign title and personal name both violate our former dynasty's taboos; the annual tribute was what your former ruler increased—now that the dynasty has changed, it should return to the Longxing and Dading precedents.'"
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens killed their ruler Yunji and enthroned a new emperor, they sent envoys to announce the succession. Some officials at once wanted to send tribute missions. Gang said: "The envoy's title is disrespectful. He should be stopped at the border. For the moment order the Left Treasury to examine precedent and make arrangements, or detain him at the Jingkou headquarters and have Chuyi instruct him: 'Your reign title and personal name both violate our dynasty's taboos. The annual tribute was increased by your former ruler. Now that the throne has changed, it should revert to the Longxing and Dading precedents.'"

sentences.zh: ’俟此議定，而後正旦、生辰之使可遣。

translations.literal: 'Wait until this matter is settled, and only then may New Year's and birthday envoys be sent.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Only after this matter is settled should envoys for New Year's Day and the emperor's birthday be dispatched.'

sentences.zh: 遲以歲月，吾擇邊將葺城堡，簡軍實，儲峙糗糧，使沿邊屹然有不可犯之勢，聽其自相攻擊，然後以全力製其後。”

translations.literal: Delay for months; we select frontier generals to repair castles and walls, streamline military realities, store provisions and dried grain, make the border stand firm with an inviolable posture, let them attack one another, and then with full strength control them from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Delay for months while we choose frontier generals to repair fortifications, streamline the army, and stock provisions, until the border stands in an posture that cannot be violated. Let them fight among themselves, and then strike with full force from behind.

sentences.zh: 廟堂韙之。

translations.literal: The court approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 提轄東西庫，又幹辦諸司審計司。

translations.literal: He supervised the Eastern and Western treasuries and also handled affairs for the Various Offices Audit Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Eastern and Western treasuries and also handled affairs for the Various Offices Audit Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以選知高郵軍，陛辭，言：“揚、楚二州當各屯二萬人，壯其聲勢，而以高郵為家計砦。

translations.literal: Through selection he became prefect of Gaoyou Command; at audience farewell he said: "Yang and Chu two prefectures should each garrison twenty thousand men to strengthen their imposing force, and take Gaoyou as the home-base fort."
translations.idiomatic: Selected as prefect of Gaoyou Command, he took leave of the emperor and said: "Yangzhou and Chuzhou should each station twenty thousand troops to strengthen their defensive posture, with Gaoyou serving as the home-base fort."

sentences.zh: 高郵三面阻水，湖澤奧阻，戎馬所不能騁，獨西南一路直距天長，無險可守，乃去城六十里隨地經畫，或浚溝塹，或備設伏，以扼其衝。”

translations.literal: Gaoyou on three sides is blocked by water; lakes and marshes are deep and obstructive; war horses cannot gallop; only the southwest route runs straight to Tianchang with no defensible terrain; he therefore went sixty li from the city to plan according to the ground—sometimes dredging ditches and moats, sometimes preparing ambushes—to choke the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyou is blocked by water on three sides; its lakes and marshes are deep and difficult, and cavalry cannot operate there. Only the southwest route runs straight toward Tianchang with no natural defenses. He therefore went sixty li from the city to plan defenses according to the terrain—dredging ditches and moats in some places, setting ambushes in others—to block the approach.

sentences.zh: 又慮湖可以入淮，招水卒五千人造百艘列三砦以戒非常。

translations.literal: He also feared that the lake could give access into the Huai; he recruited five thousand water soldiers, built a hundred vessels, and arrayed three forts to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared that the lake could provide a route into the Huai River. He recruited five thousand naval troops, built a hundred vessels, and stationed three forts as a guard against surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 興化民田濱海，昔範仲淹築堰以障寫鹵，守毛澤民置石䃮函管以疏運河水勢，歲久皆壞，綱乃增修之。

translations.literal: The people's fields of Xinghua bordered the sea; formerly Fan Zhongyan built dikes to block backflow of brine; prefect Mao Zemin set stone culvert pipes to drain the transport canal's water force; after many years all were ruined; Gang then enlarged and repaired them.
translations.idiomatic: The farmland of Xinghua bordered the sea. Fan Zhongyan had once built dikes to keep out salt tides, and prefect Mao Zemin had installed stone culverts to regulate the transport canal's flow. After many years these works had fallen into ruin, and Gang enlarged and repaired them.

sentences.zh: 部使者聞於朝，增一秩，提舉淮東常平。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy reported to court; he was raised one rank and made intendant of Huaidong Ever-Normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit envoy reported his work to court. Gang was raised one rank and appointed intendant of Huaidong Ever-Normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 淮米越江有禁，綱念“淮民有警則室廬莫保，歲凶則轉徙無歸，豐年可以少蘇，重以苛禁，自分畛域，豈為民父母意哉！

translations.literal: Huai rice crossing the Yangzi was forbidden; Gang reflected: "When Huai people have alarm, then houses cannot be preserved; in lean years they wander with nowhere to return; in abundant years they can be slightly relieved—yet with harsh prohibitions they divide into separate domains; is this the intent of parents to the people?"
translations.idiomatic: Transport of Huai rice across the Yangzi was forbidden. Gang reflected: "When alarm comes to the Huai region, homes cannot be preserved. In lean years people wander with nowhere to return. In good years they might recover a little—yet harsh prohibitions divide regions against one another. Is this how a parent official should act?"

sentences.zh: 請下金陵糴三十萬以通淮西之運，京口糴五十萬以通淮東之運。”

translations.literal: He requested that three hundred thousand be purchased at Jinling to open transport to Huai West, and five hundred thousand at Jingkou to open transport to Huai East.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that three hundred thousand piculs be purchased at Jinling to open transport to western Huai, and five hundred thousand at Jingkou to open transport to eastern Huai.

sentences.zh: 又言：“兩淮之積不可多，昇、潤之積不可少。

translations.literal: He also said: "Stores in the Two Huai cannot be too great; stores in Sheng and Run cannot be too small."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Grain reserves in the Two Huai cannot be too large, while reserves in Sheng and Run cannot be too small."

sentences.zh: 平江積米數百萬，陳陳相因，久而紅腐，宜視其收貯近久，取餉輦下百司、諸軍。

translations.literal: Pingjiang stored grain in the millions; year piled on year; after long time it turned red and rotted; one should regard how near or far and how long stored, and take it to supply the hundred offices and various armies at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang had millions of piculs in store, piled year upon year until the grain turned red and rotted. He proposed that grain be issued according to how long it had been stored, to supply the capital offices and armies.

sentences.zh: 江上歲餫當至京者，貯之京口、金陵轉漕。

translations.literal: The annual river transport due to reach the capital should be stored at Jingkou and Jinling for transfer transport.
translations.idiomatic: Annual grain transport due to reach the capital along the Yangzi should be stored at Jingkou and Jinling for relay shipment.

sentences.zh: 兩淮、中都諸倉，亦當廣糴以補其數。”

translations.literal: The various granaries of the Two Huai and the central capital region should also broadly purchase grain to supplement their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries in the Two Huai and the central capital region should also purchase grain broadly to replenish their stocks.

sentences.zh: 製置使訪綱備禦孰宜先，綱言：“淮地自昔號財賦淵藪，西有鐵冶，東富魚稻，足以自給。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner asked Gang which defense preparations should come first; Gang said: "The Huai region from old was called a deep pool of wealth and revenue; in the west there is iron smelting; in the east fish and rice are rich—enough for self-supply."
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner asked Gang which defensive measures should come first. Gang said: "The Huai region has long been called a treasury of wealth. It has ironworks in the west and abundant fish and rice in the east—enough for self-sufficiency."

sentences.zh: 淮右多山，淮左多水，足以自固。

translations.literal: Huai right has many mountains; Huai left has much water—enough for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Western Huai has many mountains and eastern Huai much water—enough for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 誠能合兩淮為一家，兵財通融，聲勢合一，雖不假江、浙之力可也。

translations.literal: If one can truly unite the Two Huai as one household, with troops and wealth flowing together and imposing force united, even without borrowing the strength of Jiang and Zhe it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If the Two Huai could truly be united as one, with troops and resources pooled and their defensive strength combined, they could hold their own even without relying on Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 祖宗盛時，邊郡所儲足支十年；

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of the ancestors, what border commanderies stored sufficed for ten years;
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's flourishing age, frontier stores sufficed for ten years;

sentences.zh: 慶曆間，中山一鎮尚百八十萬石。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era, one garrison in Zhongshan still had one million eight hundred thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingli era, a single garrison in Zhongshan still held 1.8 million piculs.

sentences.zh: 今宜上法先朝，令商旅入粟近塞，而算請錢貨於京師。

translations.literal: Now one should take the former court as model above, order merchants and travelers to bring grain into the near frontier, and calculate and request money and goods at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: We should now follow the precedents of earlier reigns: let merchants bring grain to stores near the frontier, and issue credit for money and goods at the capital.

sentences.zh: 入粟拜爵，守之以信，則輸者必多，邊儲不患不豐。

translations.literal: For bringing grain ennoblement is granted; if kept with faith, then those who deliver will surely be many, and frontier stores need not fear lacking abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Grant rank to those who deliver grain, keep faith with them, and contributors will surely multiply. Frontier stores will not lack for abundance.

sentences.zh: 州郡禁兵本非供役，乃就糧外郡耳，今不為戰鬥用，乃使之共力役，緩急戍守，專倚大軍，指日待更，不安風土，豈若土兵生長邊地，墳墓室家，人自為守邪？

translations.literal: The forbidden troops of prefectures and commanderies were originally not for corvée service but merely drew rations from outer commanderies; now they are not used for battle but made to share labor service; in urgency and ease for garrison defense they rely solely on the great army, counting days awaiting rotation, not settled in local climate—how can this compare to local troops growing up on the frontier, with graves and households, each man defending for himself?
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural forbidden troops were never meant for corvée but only drew rations from outside the circuit. Today they are not used for battle but put to labor service. In emergencies garrison defense relies solely on the main army, whose men count the days until rotation and never settle into local conditions. How can this compare to local troops raised on the frontier, with their families and ancestral graves there, defending of their own accord?

sentences.zh: 當精擇伉壯，廣其尺籍，悉隸御前軍額，分擘券給以助州郡衣糧之供，大率如山陽武鋒軍製，則邊麵不必抽江上之戍，江上不必出禁闈之師。

translations.literal: One should carefully select strong and robust men, broaden their registers, all attach them to the Imperial Front Army rolls, divide and issue certificates to assist prefectures and commanderies in clothing and grain supply—generally like the Shanyang Martial Vanguard system—then the frontier need not draw garrisons from the river, and the river need not send out forbidden-palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: Select the strongest men, expand their registers, attach them all to Imperial Front Army rolls, and issue certificates to help prefectures supply their clothing and grain—on the model of the Shanyang Martial Vanguard. Then the frontier need not draw troops from the Yangzi, and the Yangzi need not send palace guards.

sentences.zh: 生券更番，勞費俱息。”

translations.literal: With living certificates and rotating shifts, labor and expense both cease.
translations.idiomatic: With living certificates and rotating duty, labor and expense would both be reduced.

sentences.zh: 時有獻言製司廣買荒田開墾，以為營田，綱以為“荒瘠之地不難辦，而工力、水利非久不可，棄產欺官，良田終不可得，耗費公帑，開墾難就。

translations.literal: At the time someone proposed to the Pacification Commission to buy widely wasteland for opening and cultivation as garrison fields; Gang considered that "wasteland and lean soil are not hard to arrange, but labor and waterworks cannot be done quickly; abandoning property and deceiving the office, good fields ultimately cannot be obtained; public funds are wasted and opening cultivation is hard to achieve."
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone proposed that the Pacification Commission buy wasteland broadly for garrison farming. Gang argued: "Barren land is easy to obtain, but labor and irrigation cannot be completed quickly. People abandon property and deceive officials; good fields are never really secured; public funds are wasted, and reclamation fails."

sentences.zh: 曷若勸民盡耕閑田，川澮堙塞則官為之助，變瘠為沃，使民有餘蓄。

translations.literal: How much better to urge the people to fully cultivate idle fields; when streams and canals are blocked, let the government assist; change lean into fertile, and let the people have surplus stores.
translations.idiomatic: Better to urge the people to cultivate all idle fields, assist them when streams and canals are blocked, turn poor soil fertile, and let the people build up surplus stores.

sentences.zh: 晁錯入粟之議，本朝便糴之法，在其中矣。”

translations.literal: Chao Cuo's proposal for bringing in grain and this dynasty's convenient-purchase method lie within this.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo's policy of grain delivery for ennoblement and our dynasty's convenient-purchase system embody this approach.

sentences.zh: 製司知其無益，乃止。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission knew it was without benefit and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission saw that the plan was useless and abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 淮東煮鹽之利，本居天下半，歲久敝滋，鹽本日侵，帑儲空竭，負兩總司五十餘萬，亭戶二十八萬，借撥於朝廷五十萬，又會餉所復鹽鈔，舊制弗許商人預供貼鈔錢，鹽司坐是窘不能支。

translations.literal: The profit of Huaidong boiled salt originally comprised half under heaven; over years abuses increased; salt capital daily encroached; treasury stores were emptied; it owed the two general offices more than five hundred thousand; saltern households two hundred eighty thousand; borrowed and allocated from court five hundred thousand; also the commissariat restored salt certificates; the old system did not permit merchants to advance supply-note money; the salt office sat in distress unable to support.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidong's salt monopoly had once produced half the empire's revenue, but over the years abuses multiplied, capital was eroded, and the treasury was drained. The office owed the two general headquarters more than five hundred thousand strings, saltern households two hundred eighty thousand, and had borrowed five hundred thousand from court. When the commissariat restored salt certificates, the old rule forbidding merchants to advance note money left the salt office unable to meet its obligations.

sentences.zh: 綱抉擿隱伏，凡虛額無實，詭為出內，飛走移易，事製曲防，課乃更羨。

translations.literal: Gang probed and exposed what was hidden; whatever had empty quotas without reality, falsely made disbursements, flying transfers and shifts—all such schemes he bent to prevent, and the levy then became surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Gang exposed hidden abuses: empty quotas, false disbursements, and fraudulent transfers. He blocked every scheme, and revenue turned from deficit to surplus.

sentences.zh: 既盡償所負，又贏金三十萬緡，為樁辦庫，以備鹽本之闕。

translations.literal: Having fully repaid what was owed, he also gained three hundred thousand strings in gold, established a reserve treasury, to prepare for lack in salt capital.
translations.idiomatic: After repaying all debts, he still yielded three hundred thousand strings, which he placed in a reserve treasury to cover future shortfalls in salt capital.

sentences.zh: 添置新灶五十所，諸場悉視乾道舊額三百九十萬石，通一千三百萬緡，課官吏之殿最。

translations.literal: He added fifty new salterns; all stations were set to the Qiandao old quota of three million nine hundred thousand piculs, totaling thirteen million strings, and ranked officials by achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He added fifty new salterns, restored all stations to the Qiandao-era quota of 3.9 million piculs totaling thirteen million strings, and ranked officials by performance.

sentences.zh: 綱約己率下，辭台郡之互饋，獨增場官奉以養其廉。

translations.literal: Gang restrained himself and led those below; declined mutual gifts between censorial and prefectural offices; alone increased station officials' salaries to nurture their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gang practiced restraint and led by example, declined mutual gifts between censorial and prefectural offices, and alone raised station officials' salaries to support their integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部員外郎、總領淮東軍馬財賦。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and overall director of Huaidong military horses and financial levies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and appointed overall director of Huaidong military horses and financial levies.

sentences.zh: 時邊麵多生券，山東歸附月餉錢糧，以緡計增三十有三萬，米以石計增六萬，真、楚諸州又新招萬弩手，皆仰給總所，而浙西鹽利積負至七十餘萬緡，諸州漕運不以時至。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier had many living certificates; Shandong submission monthly stipends in money and grain increased by three hundred thirty thousand strings in cash and sixty thousand piculs in rice; Zhen and Chu various prefectures also newly recruited ten thousand crossbowmen—all relied on the general office for supply—while Western Zhe salt profits accumulated debt to more than seven hundred thousand strings, and various prefectures' transport did not arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier relied heavily on living certificates. Monthly stipends for Shandong submission rose by 330,000 strings and 60,000 piculs of rice. Zhen and Chu prefectures newly recruited ten thousand crossbowmen, all dependent on the general office. Meanwhile Western Zhe salt profits owed more than seven hundred thousand strings, and transport from various prefectures did not arrive on schedule.

sentences.zh: 綱核名實，警稽慢，區畫處分，餉事賴以不乏。

translations.literal: Gang verified names against reality, warned against delay in audit, planned and disposed, and provisions relied on this for not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Gang verified accounts against reality, cracked down on delays, and organized supplies so that provisions did not run short.

sentences.zh: 移疾乞閑，得直秘閣、知婺州，改提點浙東刑獄，皆屢辭不得請。

translations.literal: He reported illness and sought leisure; obtained Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou; was changed to Eastern Zhejiang judicial intendant—all repeatedly declined but requests not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported illness and asked to retire. He was appointed Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou, then judicial intendant of Eastern Zhejiang. He declined each post repeatedly but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 慮囚，至婺，有奴挾刃欲戕其主，不遇而殺其子，瞞讕妄牽連，徑出斬之。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners, arriving at Wuzhou, there was a slave who seized a blade wishing to kill his master; not meeting him he killed the son; concealment and false implication wrongly linked others; he directly ordered execution by beheading.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in Wuzhou, he found a slave who had seized a blade to kill his master, failed to find him, and killed the master's son instead. Officials had concealed the facts and falsely implicated others. Gang ordered the slave beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 釋衢囚之冤者。

translations.literal: He released those wrongly imprisoned at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He released prisoners wrongly held at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 台盜鍾百一非共盜，尉覬賞，躐申製司，綱謂：“治盜雖尚嚴，豈得鍛煉傅會以成其罪邪？”

translations.literal: A Taizhou thief Zhong Baiyi was not a co-thief; the district captain coveted reward and rashly reported to the Pacification Commission; Gang said: "Though punishing thieves should be strict, how can one forge and stitch together charges to complete the crime?"
translations.idiomatic: A thief named Zhong Baiyi in Taizhou was not an accomplice in the crime, but the district captain, coveting a reward, rashly reported to the Pacification Commission. Gang said: "Punishing thieves must be strict, but how can charges be fabricated to secure a conviction?"

sentences.zh: 於是得減死。

translations.literal: Thereupon the death sentence was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was reduced from death as a result.

sentences.zh: 禱雨龍瑞宮，有物蜿蜒朱色，盤旋壇上者三日。

translations.literal: Praying for rain at Longrui Palace, there was a thing winding in vermilion color, coiling on the altar for three days.
translations.idiomatic: While praying for rain at Longrui Palace, a vermilion serpentine creature coiled on the altar for three days.

sentences.zh: 綱曰：“吾欲雨而已，毋為異以惑眾。”

translations.literal: Gang said: "I only want rain; do not make wonders to confuse the crowd."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "I want only rain. Do not make a wonder to mislead the people."

sentences.zh: 言未竟，雷雨大至，歲以大熟。

translations.literal: Before his words ended, great thunder and rain arrived; the year had great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, a great thunderstorm broke, and the year brought an abundant harvest.

sentences.zh: 進直煥章閣、知紹興府、主管浙東安撫司公事兼提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He advanced to compiler at the Brilliant Chapter Hall, prefect of Shaoxing, in charge of Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission affairs while also judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler at the Brilliant Chapter Hall, appointed prefect of Shaoxing, placed in charge of the Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission, and also served as judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 訪民瘼，罷行尤切。

translations.literal: Inquiring into the people's afflictions, abolishing abuses was especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He inquired into the people's hardships and was especially urgent in abolishing abuses.

sentences.zh: 蕭山有古運河，西通錢塘，東達台、明，沙漲三十餘里，舟行則膠。

translations.literal: Xiaoshan had an ancient transport canal, west connecting to Qiantang, east reaching Tai and Ming; sand silted for more than thirty li; boats when traveling stuck fast.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshan had an ancient canal connecting west to Qiantang and east to Taizhou and Mingzhou. Sand had silted it for more than thirty li, and boats stuck fast.

sentences.zh: 乃開浚八千餘丈，復創閘江口，使泥淤弗得入，河水不得泄，於塗則盡甃以達城。

translations.literal: He then dredged more than eight thousand zhang, restored the sluice at the river mouth so mud silt could not enter and river water could not spill; on the road he fully paved with brick to reach the city.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged more than eight thousand zhang, rebuilt the river-mouth sluice to keep silt out and control the flow, and paved the towpath with brick all the way to the city.

sentences.zh: 十里創一廬。

translations.literal: Every ten li he created one lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He built a rest lodge every ten li.

sentences.zh: 名曰“施水 ”，主以道流。

translations.literal: It was named "Bestowing Water," managed by Daoist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: He named them "Bestowing Water" lodges and placed them under Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 於是舟車水陸，不問晝夜暑寒，意行利涉，歡欣忘勩。

translations.literal: Thereupon by boat and cart on water and land, regardless of day or night, heat or cold, travelers went as they wished with easy crossing, joyful and forgetting fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter travelers by boat and cart, by day or night and in any season, crossed with ease and forgot their fatigue in joy.

sentences.zh: 屬邑諸縣瀕海，而諸暨十六鄉瀕湖，蕩濼灌溉之利甚博，勢家巨室率私植埂岸，圍以成田，湖流既束，水不得去，雨稍多則溢入邑居，田閭浸蕩。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties all bordered the sea, while sixteen townships of Zhuji bordered the lake; the benefit of marsh irrigation was very broad; powerful families and great houses generally privately planted dikes and banks, enclosing to make fields; once lake flow was confined, water could not leave; when rain was slightly heavy it overflowed into towns and dwellings, fields and hamlets were inundated.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties bordered the sea, and sixteen townships of Zhuji bordered the lake, where marsh irrigation brought great benefit. Powerful families had privately built dikes to enclose lake land as fields. Once the lake's flow was confined, water could not drain away. After even moderate rain, towns and fields were flooded.

sentences.zh: 瀕海藉塘為固，堤岸易圮，鹹鹵害稼，歲損動數十萬畝，蠲租亦萬計。

translations.literal: Along the sea they relied on ponds for defense; dikes and banks easily collapsed; salt brine harmed crops; yearly loss often reached several hundred thousand mu; rent remissions also numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal areas relied on ponds for protection, but dikes easily collapsed and salt tides ruined crops. Tens of thousands of mu were lost each year, and rent remissions ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 以綱言，詔提舉常平司發田園，奇援巧請，一切峻卻，而湖田始復；

translations.literal: On Gang's words, an edict ordered the Ever-Normal intendant to release fields and gardens; strange pleas and clever requests were all sternly rejected, and lake fields then began to be restored;
translations.idiomatic: On Gang's recommendation, an edict ordered the Ever-Normal intendant to reclaim encroached fields. Every specious claim was sternly rejected, and lake fields began to be restored;

sentences.zh: 郡備緡錢三萬專備修築，而海田始固。

translations.literal: the prefecture prepared thirty thousand strings solely for repair and construction, and coastal fields then became secure.
translations.idiomatic: and the prefecture set aside thirty thousand strings for repairs, so that coastal fields became secure.

sentences.zh: 綱謂：“是邦控臨海道，密拱都畿，而軍籍單弱。”

translations.literal: Gang said: "This state controls the sea route and closely guards the capital region, yet military registers are thin and weak."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "This prefecture commands the sea route and closely guards the capital, yet its military rolls are thin and weak."

sentences.zh: 乃招水軍，刺叉手，教習甚專，不令他役。

translations.literal: He then recruited naval troops, branded fork-handlers, trained them very exclusively, and did not assign other duties.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited naval troops and fork-handlers, trained them intensively, and assigned them no other duties.

sentences.zh: 創營千餘間，寬整堅密，增置甲兵，威聲赫然。

translations.literal: He created more than a thousand barracks, broad, orderly, solid and tight; increased armor and weapons; imposing reputation blazed.
translations.idiomatic: He built more than a thousand spacious, solid barracks, increased armor and weapons, and his military reputation became formidable.

sentences.zh: 兼權司農卿，尋直龍圖閣，因任。

translations.literal: He concurrently acted as Minister of Agriculture; soon was made compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall and continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as acting Minister of Agriculture, then was made compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，詔為右文殿修撰，加集英殿修撰，復因任，又加寶謨閣待制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was ordered Right Culture Hall compiler, advanced to Hall for Assembling Excellence compiler, again continued in office, and further made Baomo Pavilion attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, Gang was appointed Right Culture Hall compiler, promoted to Hall for Assembling Excellence compiler, continued in office, and further made Baomo Pavilion attendant.

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年大水，綱發粟三萬八千餘、緡錢五萬振之，蠲租六萬餘石，捐瘠頓蘇，無異常歲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing great flood; Gang released more than thirty-eight thousand piculs of grain and fifty thousand strings to relieve; remitted rent of more than sixty thousand piculs; the emaciated suddenly revived, no different from a normal year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing a great flood struck. Gang distributed more than thirty-eight thousand piculs of grain and fifty thousand strings for relief, remitted more than sixty thousand piculs of rent, and the starving were suddenly revived as in a normal year.

sentences.zh: 越有經總製窠名四十一萬，其中二十五，則紹興以來虛額也，前後帥懼負殿，以修奉欑宮之資偽增焉。

translations.literal: Yue had general aggregate account items of four hundred ten thousand, of which two hundred fifty thousand were empty quotas since Shaoxing; successive prefects feared failing targets and falsely increased them with funds for repairing and supplying the spirit palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had general aggregate account items totaling 410,000 strings, of which 250,000 were empty quotas dating from the Shaoxing era. Successive prefects, fearing shortfalls, had falsely inflated them with funds nominally for repairing the spirit palaces.

sentences.zh: 綱謂：“負殿之責小，罔上之罪大”。

translations.literal: Gang said: "The blame for missing targets is small; the crime of deceiving superiors is great."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Falling short of targets is a small fault; deceiving superiors is a great crime."

sentences.zh: 摭其實以聞。

translations.literal: He gathered the facts and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the facts and reported them to court.

sentences.zh: 詔免九萬五千緡，而宿敝因是著明矣。

translations.literal: An edict remitted ninety-five thousand strings, and long-standing abuses thereby became clear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted ninety-five thousand strings, and long-standing abuses were thereby exposed.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，召赴行在，綱入見，言：“臣下先利之心過於徇義，為身之計過於謀國，俞惰退縮，奔競貪黷，相與為欺，宜有以轉移之。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was summoned to the traveling residence; Gang entered audience and said: "Subjects' hearts putting profit first exceed following righteousness; plans for the self exceed planning for the state; compliance, laziness, retreat, and shrinkage, rushing competition and greedy corruption—they deceive one another; there should be means to shift this."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding he was summoned to the temporary capital. At audience Gang said: "Officials put profit before duty and personal interest before the state. Compliance, laziness, retreat, and corruption prevail, and they deceive one another. Something must be done to change this."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“聞卿治行甚美，越中民力如何？”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have heard your governance and conduct are very fine—how is the people's strength in Yuezhong?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have heard your governance is excellent. How are the people faring in Yue?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“ 去歲水潦，諸暨為甚，今歲幸中熟，十年之間，千里晏安，皆朝廷威德所及，臣何力之有。”

translations.literal: He replied: "Last year flood and waterlogging, Zhuji suffered most; this year fortunately mid-harvest; within ten years, a thousand li at peace—all reached by the court's awesome virtue; what strength have I?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Last year there were floods, and Zhuji suffered most. This year we have had a fair harvest. For ten years the region has been at peace—all through the court's virtue. What strength have I?"

sentences.zh: 權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 越數月，上章致仕，特畀二秩，守戶部侍郎，仍賜金帶。

translations.literal: After several months he submitted a memorial to retire; specially granted two ranks; retained as Vice Minister of Revenue; still bestowed a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he memorialized to retire. He was specially granted two ranks, retained as Vice Minister of Revenue, and given a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 卒，越人聞之多墮淚，有相率哭於寺觀者。

translations.literal: He died; when the people of Yue heard, many shed tears; some together went to weep at temples and shrines.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, many in Yue shed tears on hearing the news, and some gathered to weep at temples and shrines.

sentences.zh: 綱學有本原，多聞博記，兵農、醫卜、陰陽、律曆諸書，靡不研究；

translations.literal: Gang's learning had root and origin; he heard much and recorded broadly; military agriculture, medicine and divination, yin-yang, pitch pipes and calendars—all books he studied without exception;
translations.idiomatic: Gang's learning had deep foundations. He was widely read and had studied every subject—military affairs and agriculture, medicine and divination, yin-yang theory, music, and calendrics;

sentences.zh: 機神明銳，遇事立決。

translations.literal: his mind was spirit-bright and sharp; encountering affairs he decided at once.
translations.idiomatic: his mind was keen and sharp, and he decided affairs on the spot.

sentences.zh: 在越佩四印，文書山積，而能操約禦詳，治事不過二十刻，公庭如水。

translations.literal: In Yue he wore four seals; documents piled like mountains, yet he could hold to brevity to control detail; handling affairs took no more than twenty quarter-hours; the public court was like water.
translations.idiomatic: In Yue he held four seals at once. Though documents piled like mountains, he governed with concise control of detail, finished business in no more than twenty quarter-hours, and kept the public court as calm as still water.

sentences.zh: 卑官下吏，一言中理，慨然從之。

translations.literal: For humble officials and lower clerks, if one word hit principle, he generously followed it.
translations.idiomatic: If a humble official or clerk spoke one word that hit the mark, he readily accepted it.

sentences.zh: 為文尤長於論事，援據古今，辨博雄勁。

translations.literal: In writing he especially excelled at discussing affairs, citing past and present, argumentative, broad, bold and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he excelled at policy argument, citing past and present with forceful, expansive eloquence.

sentences.zh: 服用不喜奢麗，供帳車剩，雖敝不更。

translations.literal: In dress and use he did not like luxury; provision accounts and carriage surplus—even if worn he did not replace.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked luxury in dress and furnishings. His carriage and equipment he would not replace even when worn.

sentences.zh: 所著有《恕齋集》、《左帑志》、《漫存錄》。

translations.literal: His writings included Collection of the Forgiving Studio, Record of the Left Treasury, and Random Preserved Records.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Collection of the Forgiving Studio, Record of the Left Treasury, and Random Preserved Records.

sentences.zh: 陳宓，字師復，丞相俊卿之子。

translations.literal: Chen Mi, styled Shifu, was the son of Chief Councilor Junqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mi, styled Shifu, was the son of Chief Councilor Chen Junqing.

sentences.zh: 少嚐及登朱熹之門，熹器異之。

translations.literal: In youth he once reached Zhu Xi's gate; Xi regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Zhu Xi, who regarded him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 長從黃幹遊。

translations.literal: Growing up he followed Huang Gan in study.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied with Huang Gan.

sentences.zh: 以父任曆泉州南安鹽稅，主管南外睦宗院、再主管西外，知安溪縣。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he successively served as Nan'an salt tax officer in Quanzhou, supervised the Southern Outer Muzong Court, again supervised the Western Outer, and was magistrate of Anxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he served as salt-tax officer in Nan'an, Quanzhou, supervised the Southern and Western Outer Muzong Courts in turn, and was appointed magistrate of Anxi County.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，入監進奏院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he entered as supervisor of the Memorial Transmission Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiading (1214) he entered service as supervisor of the Memorial Transmission Court.

sentences.zh: 時無敢慷慨盡言者，宓上封事言：“宮中宴飲或至無節，非時賜予為數浩穰，一人蔬食而嬪禦不廢於擊鮮，邊事方殷而樁積反資於妄用，此宮闈儀刑有未正也。

translations.literal: At the time none dared speak generously to the full; Mi submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Palace banquets and drinking sometimes reach without limit; untimely bestowals are numerous and vast; one man eats vegetables while consorts do not cease striking fresh food; frontier affairs are just urgent yet piled stores instead supply reckless use—here palace ritual and punishment are not yet corrected."
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one dared speak boldly. Mi submitted a sealed memorial: "Palace feasting sometimes knows no limit. Untimely gifts are lavished in vast numbers. The emperor eats frugally while consorts still demand fresh delicacies. The frontier is in crisis yet stored supplies are squandered. Palace discipline has not been set right."

sentences.zh: 大臣所用非親即故，執政擇易製之人，台諫用慎默之士，都司樞掾，無非親昵，貪吏靡不得誌，廉士動招怨尤，此朝廷權柄有所分也。

translations.literal: Those whom great ministers employ are none but kin or old associates; those in power choose men easy to control; remonstrators and censors use cautious and silent scholars; capital bureau and military affairs clerks are all without exception intimates; greedy officials none fail to get their will; upright men constantly invite blame—here court authority is divided.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers appoint only kin or old associates. Those in power choose men easy to control. Censors select the cautious and silent. Capital and military clerks are all intimates. Greedy officials always get their way; upright men invite resentment. Court authority has been divided up."

sentences.zh: 鈔鹽變易，楮幣秤提，安邊所創立，固執己見，動失人心，敗軍之將躐躋殿岩，庸鄙之夫久尹京兆，宿將有守成之功，以小過而貶，三牙無汗馬之勞，托公勤而擢，此政令刑賞多所舛逆也。

translations.literal: Salt certificates changed, paper money weighed and raised, frontier pacification offices newly established—they stubbornly hold their own views and constantly lose popular hearts; defeated generals leap to palace halls; vulgar and base men long govern the capital; veteran generals with merit in holding what was gained are demoted for small faults; the three guards without sweat-horse labor are promoted under plea of public diligence—here government orders, punishments and rewards mostly run contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Salt certificates are changed, paper money manipulated, frontier offices created—officials cling to their own views and constantly lose popular support. Defeated generals leap to high office. Vulgar men long govern the capital. Veteran generals who held the line are demoted for minor faults. Palace guards without battlefield merit are promoted for pretended diligence. Commands, punishments, and rewards run contrary to justice.

sentences.zh: 若能交飭內外，一正紀綱，天且不雨，臣請伏麵謾之罪。”

translations.literal: If one can jointly admonish inside and outside and unify correction of discipline, if heaven still does not rain, your subject requests to submit to the crime of lying face down in noodles.
translations.idiomatic: If inside and outside can be disciplined and order restored, and heaven still withholds rain, I ask to accept the punishment for lying to the throne.

sentences.zh: 奏入，丞相史彌遠不樂，而中宮慶壽，三牙獻遺，至是為之罷卻。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was displeased; but the inner palace was celebrating longevity, and the three guards presented gifts—on this account these were stopped and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was displeased. But the empress was celebrating her birthday and the three guards were presenting gifts—and on this account those gifts were halted.

sentences.zh: 尋遷軍器監簿。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to registrar of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to registrar of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉對言：

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at rotation audience he spoke:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at his rotation audience he said:

sentences.zh: 人主之德貴乎明，大臣之心貴乎公，台諫之言貴乎直。

translations.literal: The ruler's virtue values clarity; the great minister's heart values fairness; the censor's and remonstrator's words value directness.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's virtue lies in clarity, the minister's heart in fairness, and the censor's words in directness.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨政雖勤而治功未舉，奉身雖儉而財用未豐，愛民雖仁而實惠未遍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty governs diligently yet governing achievement is not raised; personally you are frugal yet finances are not abundant; you love the people benevolently yet real benefit is not widespread.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs diligently yet achievement is not realized. You are personally frugal yet revenues are not ample. You love the people yet real benefit does not reach them.

sentences.zh: 良由上下相蒙，務於欺蔽。

translations.literal: Truly because above and below deceive one another, they devote themselves to concealment.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly because superiors and subordinates deceive one another and devote themselves to concealment.

sentences.zh: 匭奏囊封，有懷畢吐，陛下付近臣差擇，是有意於行其言也。

translations.literal: Box memorials and sealed pouches—those with feelings speak fully; Your Majesty entrusts nearby ministers to select and differentiate—this shows intent to carry out their words.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials in the suggestion box and sealed pouches allow people to speak fully. Your Majesty entrusts nearby ministers to select among them—showing intent to act on what is said.

sentences.zh: 而有司惟取專攻上躬與移咎牧守之章，騰播中外，以答觀聽。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible offices only take chapters specially attacking the sovereign's person and shifting blame to prefects and shepherds, spreading them inside and outside to answer what is seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices take only memorials attacking the emperor personally or shifting blame to local officials, spread them throughout the realm, and present them as the government's response.

sentences.zh: 今赤地千里，蝗飛蔽天，如此其可畏，猶或諱晦以旱不為災、蝗不害稼，其他誣罔，抑又可知。

translations.literal: Now red earth for a thousand li, locusts flying covering the sky—so fearful as this—yet some still conceal and say drought is not disaster, locusts do not harm crops; other falsehoods and deception may likewise be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now the land is parched for a thousand li and locusts darken the sky. Yet some still conceal the truth, claiming drought is no disaster and locusts do not harm crops. Other deceptions may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰人主之德貴乎明。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says the ruler's virtue values clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say the ruler's virtue lies in clarity.

sentences.zh: 大臣施設，浸異厥初。

translations.literal: Great ministers' measures gradually differ from their beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers' conduct has gradually diverged from their beginnings.

sentences.zh: 凡建議求言之人，則以他事逐，諫官言事稍直，則以他職徙。

translations.literal: Whoever proposed seeking words is driven off on other matters; remonstrating officials whose words are slightly direct are moved to other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who proposed seeking candid advice are driven off on other grounds. Remonstrating officials who speak too directly are transferred to other posts.

sentences.zh: 忠憤者指為不靖，切直者目曰沽名，眾怨所萃則相繼超升，物論所歸則以次疏外。

translations.literal: The loyal and indignant are pointed to as unrestful; the cutting and direct are eyed as fishing for fame; where popular resentment gathers they are successively promoted; where public opinion inclines they are in order sent outside.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and indignant are labeled disloyal. The blunt and direct are accused of seeking fame. Those whom popular resentment targets are promoted in succession. Those whom public opinion favors are gradually pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 某人之遷，是嚐重人罪以快同列之私忿者；

translations.literal: A certain person's transfer was one who once aggravated others' crimes to satisfy colleagues' private resentment;
translations.idiomatic: One man's promotion was of someone who had once inflated others' crimes to satisfy colleagues' private grudges;

sentences.zh: 某人之擢，是嚐援古事以文邇日之天變者。

translations.literal: a certain person's elevation was one who once cited ancient affairs to ornament recent heaven's changes.
translations.idiomatic: another's promotion was of someone who had cited ancient precedents to gloss over recent heavenly portents.

sentences.zh: 直節重望以私嫌而久棄，老奸宿臧以巧請而牽復。

translations.literal: Upright integrity and heavy reputation are long cast aside for private dislike; old traitors and long-standing villains are drawn back through clever pleas.
