translations.idiomatic: Men of upright integrity and high reputation are long cast aside for private dislike, while old traitors and long-standing villains are restored through clever pleas.

sentences.zh: 使大臣果能杜幸門、塞邪徑，則舉錯當而人心服。

translations.literal: If great ministers truly could block the gate of favor and stop evil paths, then rises and falls would be fitting and people's hearts would submit.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers truly blocked the gate of favoritism and closed evil paths, appointments would be fitting and hearts would be won.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰大臣之心貴乎公。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says the great minister's heart values fairness.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say the minister's heart lies in fairness.

sentences.zh: 台諫平居未嚐立異，遇事不敢盡言。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators in normal times have not stood apart; encountering affairs they dare not speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators in normal times never stand apart. When affairs arise they dare not speak fully.

sentences.zh: 有如金人再通，最關國體，近而侍從，下至生徒，莫不力爭，冀裨廟算，獨於言責，不出一辭。

translations.literal: Such as when the Jurchens communicated again—most related to national substance—from nearby attendants down to students, all strive and contend, hoping to aid court planning—only those with the duty of speech did not utter one word.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens reopened relations—a matter most vital to the state—attendants and students alike argued forcefully to aid court policy. Only those charged with remonstrance did not utter a word.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，乾沒巨萬，莫之誰何；

translations.literal: Under the imperial carriage hub, embezzlement reached tens of thousands—no one could do anything;
translations.idiomatic: Under the capital, embezzlement reached tens of thousands—no one could touch the culprits;

sentences.zh: 州縣之間，罪僅毫髮，摭以塞責。

translations.literal: between prefectures and counties, guilt was only a hair's breadth yet was picked up to fill responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: while in the prefectures and counties, the slightest fault was seized upon to satisfy quotas.

sentences.zh: 大臣所欲為之事則遂之，所不右之人則排之。

translations.literal: What great ministers wished to do was carried through; those they did not favor were pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: What ministers wished to do was carried through; those they disfavored were pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，有宰相奉行台諫風旨之譏，今乃有台諫不敢違中書之誚，豈祖宗設官之初意哉？

translations.literal: In Emperor Renzong's time there was the ridicule of a chief councilor following censors' and remonstrators' wind and intent; now there is the mockery that censors and remonstrators dare not violate the Secretariat—is this the original intent when the ancestors established offices?
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong there was ridicule of a chief councilor who followed censors' lead. Now there is mockery that censors dare not disobey the Secretariat. Is this what the founders intended when they established these offices?

sentences.zh: 臣故曰台諫之言貴乎直。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says censors' and remonstrators' words value directness.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say the censor's words lie in directness.

sentences.zh: 三者機括所係，願陛下幡然悔悟，昭明德以照臨百官。

translations.literal: These three are where the pivot and handle are tied; may Your Majesty suddenly repent and awaken, make bright virtue to shine on and oversee the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: These three matters are where the pivot lies. May Your Majesty repent and make your virtue shine forth to oversee all officials.

sentences.zh: 大臣、台諫，亦宜公心直節，以副望治之意。

translations.literal: Great ministers and censorial remonstrators should also use fair hearts and upright integrity to answer the intent of hoping for good government.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and censors should also act with fair hearts and upright integrity to fulfill the hope for good government.

sentences.zh: 指陳敝事，視前疏尤剴切焉。

translations.literal: Pointing out and presenting abuses, compared with the former memorial it was especially forceful and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: In pointing out abuses, this memorial was even more forceful and cutting than his earlier one.

sentences.zh: 宓遂請罷，歸。

translations.literal: Mi then requested dismissal and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then asked to be dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 在告日，擢太府丞，不拜，出知南康軍。

translations.literal: On days of leave he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury; he did not accept and went out as prefect of Nankang Command.
translations.idiomatic: While on leave he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury but declined the post and was appointed prefect of Nankang Command.

sentences.zh: 詣史彌遠別，彌遠曰：“子言甚切當，第愚昧不能行，殊有愧耳。”

translations.literal: He went to take leave of Shi Miyuan; Miyuan said: "Your words are very forceful and fitting, only I am foolish and cannot carry them out—I am especially ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: When he went to bid farewell to Shi Miyuan, Miyuan said, "Your words are forceful and apt, but I am too foolish to act on them. I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 至官，歲大侵，奏蠲其賦十之九。

translations.literal: Arriving at his post, the year had great invasion; he memorialized remitting nine-tenths of the tax.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he found the year had brought severe crop failure. He memorialized to remit nine-tenths of the tax levy.

sentences.zh: 會流民群集，宓就役之，築江堤，而給其食。

translations.literal: When displaced people gathered in crowds, Mi put them to corvée, built river dikes, and gave them food.
translations.idiomatic: When refugees gathered in crowds, he put them to work building river dikes and provided them with food.

sentences.zh: 時造白鹿洞，與諸生討論。

translations.literal: At the time he built the White Deer Grotto and discussed with the students.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the White Deer Grotto Academy and debated the classics with his students.

sentences.zh: 改知南劍州。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Nanjian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 時大旱疫，蠲逋賦十數萬，且弛新輸三之一，躬率僚吏持錢粟藥餌戶給之。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought and plague; he remitted overdue levies of several hundred thousand and also relaxed one-third of new payments; personally leading aides and clerks he took money, grain, and medicine door to door to give.
translations.idiomatic: There was severe drought and plague. He remitted overdue taxes totaling several hundred thousand strings, reduced new levies by one-third, and personally led his staff door to door distributing money, grain, and medicine.

sentences.zh: 創延平書院，悉仿白鹿洞之規。

translations.literal: He created Yanping Academy, entirely imitating the White Deer Grotto regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Yanping Academy, following the White Deer Grotto regulations in full.

sentences.zh: 知漳州，未行，聞寧宗崩，嗚咽累日。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Zhangzhou; before departing he heard Emperor Ningzong had died and sobbed for many days.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Zhangzhou but had not yet departed when he heard that Emperor Ningzong had died. He sobbed for many days.

sentences.zh: 亡何，請致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，提點廣東刑獄，章復三上，迄不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing he was made judicial intendant of Guangdong; memorials were submitted three times; he never took the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoqing he was appointed judicial intendant of Guangdong. He submitted three memorials declining the post and never took office.

sentences.zh: 直秘閣，主管崇禧觀，宓拜祠命而辭職名。

translations.literal: Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion, in charge of Chongxi Observatory; Mi accepted the temple appointment but declined the official title.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin compiler in the Secretariat Pavilion and placed in charge of Chongxi Observatory. He accepted the temple appointment but declined the official title.

sentences.zh: 卒，進職一等致仕。

translations.literal: He died; his rank was advanced one grade for retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his rank was advanced one grade in recognition of retirement.

sentences.zh: 三學諸生以起宓為請，而沒已閱月矣。

translations.literal: Students of the Three Academies petitioned to recall Mi, but he had already been dead a month.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Three Academies petitioned to recall Mi to office, but he had already been dead for a month.

sentences.zh: 初，宓之在朝也，寺丞丁焴往使金，宓歎曰：“世仇未復，何以好為？”

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mi was at court, Vice Director Ding Huang went as envoy to Jin; Mi sighed and said: "The age-old enemy is not yet avenged—how can one act cordially?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Mi was at court, Vice Director Ding Huang was sent as envoy to the Jin. Mi sighed and said, "Our hereditary enemy is not yet avenged. How can we act cordially?"

sentences.zh: 餞詩有“百年中國豈無人”之句。

translations.literal: In his farewell poem there was the line "In a hundred years can China truly have no men?"
translations.idiomatic: In his farewell poem he wrote the line, "In a hundred years can China truly have no men?"

sentences.zh: 後數年，聞關外不靖，以書抵焴曰：“蜀口去關外雖遠，實如一身。

translations.literal: Several years later, hearing the area outside the passes was not tranquil, he wrote to Huang: "The Shu mouth though far from outside the passes is in reality like one body."
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, hearing that the region beyond the passes was unsettled, he wrote to Huang: "Though Shu is far from the frontier passes, they are in reality one body."

sentences.zh: 近事可寒心，皆士大夫之罪，豈非賄道不絕之故耶？”

translations.literal: Recent affairs are heart-chilling—all are the crimes of scholar-officials; is it not because the path of bribery never ceases?
translations.idiomatic: Recent events are chilling to the heart. They are all the fault of scholar-officials. Is this not because the path of bribery never ceases?

sentences.zh: 焴服其言。

translations.literal: Huang was convinced by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was convinced by his words.

sentences.zh: 宓天性剛毅，信道尤篤，嚐為《朱墨銘》，謂朱屬陽，墨屬陰，以驗理欲分寸之多寡。

translations.literal: Mi by nature was firm and resolute, believing the Way especially devoutly; he once made An Inscription on Vermilion and Ink, saying vermilion belongs to yang and ink to yin, to test the more or less of principle and desire by minute measure.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was by nature firm and resolute and especially devout in his faith. He once wrote An Inscription on Vermilion and Ink, saying that vermilion belongs to yang and ink to yin, using them to measure the balance between principle and desire.

sentences.zh: 自言居官必如顏真卿，居家必如陶潛，而深愛諸葛亮身死家無餘財，庫無餘帛。

translations.literal: He said himself that in office one must be like Yan Zhenqing, at home like Tao Qian, and deeply loved Zhuge Liang—when his body died the family had no surplus wealth, the treasury no surplus cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He said that in office one must be like Yan Zhenqing, at home like Tao Qian, and he deeply admired Zhuge Liang, who at death left his family no surplus wealth and the treasury no surplus cloth.

sentences.zh: 庶乎能蹈其語者，端平初，殿中侍御史王遂首言：“宓事先帝有論諫之直，而不及俟聖化之更，宜褒其身後，以勸天下之為臣者。”

translations.literal: Perhaps able to tread his words—at the beginning of Duanping, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Sui first spoke: "Mi served the former emperor with the directness of remonstrance and discussion, yet did not wait to see the sage transformation renewed—he should be honored after death to encourage all under heaven who serve as subjects."
translations.idiomatic: Whether he truly lived up to his words, at the beginning of the Duanping reign Palace Attendant Censor Wang Sui was the first to speak: "Mi served the former emperor with forthright remonstrance but did not live to see the renewal of sage rule. He should be honored after death to encourage all who serve as subjects under heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝為感動，詔贈直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and ordered him posthumously granted compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and ordered him posthumously granted the title of compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《論語注義問答》、《春秋三傳抄》、《讀通鑒綱目》、《唐史贅疣》之稿數十卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: His written works included Questions and Answers on the Meaning of the Analects Commentary, Extracts of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, Reading the Comprehensive Mirror Outline, and drafts of Excrescences on Tang History in several tens of chapters, stored in his household.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Questions and Answers on the Meaning of the Analects Commentary, Extracts of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, Reading the Comprehensive Mirror Outline, and drafts of Excrescences on Tang History in several tens of chapters, kept in his household.

sentences.zh: 王霆，字定叟，東陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Ting, styled Dingsou, was a man of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ting, styled Dingsou, was a native of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 高大父豪，帥眾誅方臘，以功補官。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wang Hao led the masses to execute Fang La and through merit received supplemental office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wang Hao had led troops to suppress Fang La and received an official appointment for his merit.

sentences.zh: 霆少有奇氣，試有司不偶，去就武舉，嘉定四年，中絕倫異等。

translations.literal: Ting in youth had unusual spirit; testing at the civil service he did not succeed; he left and took the military examination; in the fourth year of Jiading he passed the peerless extraordinary grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ting in youth had an unusual spirit. He failed the civil service examination, turned to the military examination, and in the fourth year of Jiading passed at the peerless extraordinary grade.

sentences.zh: 喬行簡考藝別頭，喜曰：“吾為朝廷得一帥才矣。”

translations.literal: Qiao Xingjian examined arts as separate head and said with joy: "I have obtained a commander talent for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian, examining candidates as chief examiner, said with delight, "I have found a commander for the court."

sentences.zh: 授承節郎，從軍於鄂，帥鍾興嗣戍邊，請於樞密院，以霆為隨軍都錢糧官。

translations.literal: He was granted Bearer of Credentials; he followed the army at E; commander Zhong Xingsi garrisoned the frontier and requested from the Bureau of Military Affairs that Ting serve as overall army funds-and-grain officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the rank of Bearer of Credentials and joined the army at Ezhou. Commander Zhong Xingsi, garrisoning the frontier, requested from the Bureau of Military Affairs that Ting serve as army funds-and-grain officer.

sentences.zh: 總領綦奎委霆專一教閱總效軍，尋委帥師守禦黃州。

translations.literal: Overall director Qi Kui entrusted Ting solely to train and review the General Effectiveness Army; soon he was entrusted to command troops to defend Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Overall director Qi Kui entrusted Ting solely with training and reviewing the General Effectiveness Army. Soon he was entrusted to command troops defending Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 沿江製置副使李埴辟置幕下，淮右兵叛，遣霆招諭之。

translations.literal: Vice Pacification Commissioner along the river Li Fu recruited him to his staff; Huai-right troops rebelled and he sent Ting to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Pacification Commissioner along the Yangzi Li Fu recruited him to his staff. When troops in western Huai rebelled, Li sent Ting to summon and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 霆於軍事知無不言，謂：“招募良家子，不可以寅緣關節冒濫其間，防守江麵，全藉正軍，若義勇、民兵，特可為聲援耳。

translations.literal: Ting on military affairs knew nothing he did not speak of, saying: "Recruiting sons of good households—one cannot through connections and favoritism let them flood in; defending the river surface relies entirely on regular troops; volunteer and militia forces can only serve as vocal support."
translations.idiomatic: On military affairs Ting held nothing back. He said: "When recruiting sons of good households, one must not let connections and favoritism flood the ranks. Defending the Yangzi depends entirely on regular troops. Volunteers and militia can serve only as vocal support."

sentences.zh: 而所謂大軍，羸病者多，兵械損舊，豈不敗事。

translations.literal: Yet the so-called great army has many weak and sick; weapons damaged and old—how can affairs not fail?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the so-called main army has many weak and sick men, and its weapons are damaged and worn. How can this not lead to defeat?

sentences.zh: 調兵防江，當於江岸創屋居之，使之專心守禦。

translations.literal: Transferring troops to defend the river, one should create houses on the river bank for them to dwell in, causing them to concentrate on defense.
translations.idiomatic: Troops transferred to defend the river should be housed on the riverbank so they can concentrate on defense.

sentences.zh: 諸軍伍法既廢，平居則無以稽其虛籍冒請之敝，無以糾其竄逸生事之人，緩急則無以稽其並力向敵之誌，無以連其逃陳不進之心。

translations.literal: Since the various armies' company regulations were abolished, in normal times there is no means to audit the abuses of empty registers and false claims, no means to correct those who flee and stir trouble; in urgency and ease there is no means to audit their will to combine strength against the enemy, no means to link their hearts that flee the formation and do not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Since company regulations have been abandoned, in peacetime there is no way to audit empty registers and false claims or correct deserters who stir trouble. In emergencies there is no way to test their will to fight together or bind those who flee the line and refuse to advance.

sentences.zh: 此尉繚子所以著束部伍之令，太公謂伍法為要者謂此也。

translations.literal: This is why Master Wei Liao wrote the order binding companies and squads; when the Grand Duke said company law was essential, he meant this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Master Wei Liao wrote orders binding companies and squads, and why the Grand Duke called company law essential.

sentences.zh: 用兵不以人數多寡為勝負，惟教習之精否，則勝負之形可見矣。”

translations.literal: Using troops does not take multitude or fewness of numbers for victory and defeat; only whether training and drill are refined or not—then the form of victory and defeat can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Victory in war does not depend on numbers but on whether training and drill are thorough. Then the outcome can be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 大帥薦之，召試為閣門舍人。

translations.literal: The great commander recommended him; he was summoned for examination as Gate Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The commander recommended him, and he was summoned for examination as Gate Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 入對言：“恢復之說有二：曰規模，曰機會。

translations.literal: Entering audience he spoke: "The theory of recovery has two aspects: called planning, called opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said, "The theory of recovery has two aspects: planning and opportunity."

sentences.zh: 顧今日之規模安在哉？

translations.literal: But where is today's planning?
translations.idiomatic: But where is today's planning?

sentences.zh: 守令所以牧民，而惠養之未加；

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are to shepherd the people, yet fostering care is not added;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are meant to govern the people, yet benevolent care is not extended to them;

sentences.zh: 將帥所以禦軍，而拊循之未至。

translations.literal: generals are to control the army, yet comforting and guiding have not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: generals are meant to command the army, yet they do not comfort and guide their troops.

sentences.zh: 邦財未裕，而楮券之敝浸深；

translations.literal: State wealth is not ample, yet the abuses of paper notes grow deeper;
translations.idiomatic: State finances are not ample, yet the abuses of paper money grow worse;

sentences.zh: 軍儲未豐，而和糴之害徒慘。

translations.literal: military stores are not abundant, yet the harm of harmonized purchase is only cruel.
translations.idiomatic: military stores are not abundant, yet the harm of government grain purchases grows only more cruel.

sentences.zh: 官有土地而荒蕪，民因賦役而破蕩，獄訟類成冤抑，銓曹率多淹留。

translations.literal: The government has land yet it lies waste; the people because of tax and corvée are broken and ruined; prison cases mostly become wrongful suppression; the selection bureau mostly has many detained.
translations.idiomatic: Government land lies waste. The people are ruined by taxes and corvée. Court cases mostly end in wrongful conviction. The selection bureau mostly delays appointments.

sentences.zh: 薦舉無反坐，貪徒得以引類而通班；

translations.literal: Recommendations have no counter-penalty; greedy fellows can draw their kind and pass into court ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations carry no penalty for falsehood, so the greedy draw their kind into office;

sentences.zh: 按刺不徇公，微官易以迕意而連譴。

translations.literal: investigations do not follow fairness; humble officials are easily punished in chains for offending intent.
translations.idiomatic: investigations are not impartial, and humble officials are easily punished in chains for giving offense.

sentences.zh: 以言郡計，則紛耗於囊橐包苴；

translations.literal: Speaking of prefectural accounts, they are scattered and wasted on purses and wrapped bribes;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of prefectural accounts, they are wasted on bribery;

sentences.zh: 以言戰功，則多私於親昵故舊。

translations.literal: speaking of battle merit, it mostly goes privately to intimates and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: speaking of battle merit, it mostly goes to intimates and old friends.

sentences.zh: 至如降卒中處，養虎遺患，輕敵開邊，以肉喂虎。

translations.literal: As for settling surrendered troops in the interior, nurturing tigers and leaving calamity, treating the enemy lightly and opening the frontier—feeding tigers with flesh.
translations.idiomatic: As for settling surrendered troops in the interior, it nurtures tigers and leaves calamity behind. Treating the enemy lightly and opening the frontier is feeding tigers with flesh.

sentences.zh: 夫以規模之切要者而不滿人意如此，臣敢輕進恢復之說以誤上聽哉？

translations.literal: That planning's most urgent points should so fail to satisfy people's hearts—how dare your subject lightly advance the theory of recovery to mislead what the sovereign hears?
translations.idiomatic: When planning itself is so unsatisfactory, how dare I lightly advance a theory of recovery to mislead Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 凡臣之所陳者，誠播告中外之臣，悉懲其舊而圖其新。

translations.literal: All that your subject has presented—truly broadcast and tell officials inside and outside, all punish their old ways and plan their new.
translations.idiomatic: What I have presented should be broadcast to all officials within and without, that they may abandon old abuses and plan anew.

sentences.zh: 規模既立，然後義旗一麾，諸道並進，臣力尚壯，願效前驅。

translations.literal: Once planning is established, then with righteous banner once waved, all circuits advance together; your subject's strength is still robust; he wishes to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Once planning is established, then with the righteous banner raised all circuits may advance together. My strength is still robust, and I wish to serve in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下堅定而勉圖之。”

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty be firm and strive to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that Your Majesty be firm and strive to achieve it.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其言可采。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words as adoptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words as worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 升武功大夫，出知濠州，賜金帶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Martial Achievement Grandee and sent out as prefect of Haozhou; a gold belt was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Martial Achievement Grandee, appointed prefect of Haozhou, and granted a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 至州，節浮費，糴粟買馬，以備不虞。

translations.literal: Arriving at the prefecture, he cut floating expenses, purchased grain and bought horses to prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture, he cut unnecessary expenses, purchased grain, and bought horses to prepare against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 尋差知安豐軍，臣僚上言：“王霆在濠，人甚安之，不宜輕易。”

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned prefect of Anfeng Command; officials memorialized: "Wang Ting at Hao—the people are very settled; he should not be lightly changed."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to Anfeng Command. Officials memorialized: "The people are very settled under Wang Ting at Hao. He should not be lightly transferred."

sentences.zh: 詔再任濠，職事修舉，特轉橫班。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to serve again at Hao; official duties were raised and carried out; he was specially transferred to the lateral ranks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to serve again at Hao. He carried out his duties well and was specially promoted within the lateral ranks.

sentences.zh: 諸使交薦之。

translations.literal: Various commissioners repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Various commissioners repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 北兵至浮光，其民奔遁，相屬於道，朝論以為霆可守之，乃知光州兼沿邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Northern troops reached Fuguang; its people fled in panic, following one another on the road; court discussion held that Ting could defend it; he was made prefect of Guangzhou while also frontier overall patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops reached Fuguang, its people fled in panic along the roads. Court opinion held that Ting could hold the place, and he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou while also serving as frontier overall patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冒雪夜行，倍道疾馳至州，分遣間探，整飭戰守之具，大戰於謝令橋，光人遂安。

translations.literal: Braving snow he traveled by night, doubling the road and galloping fast to the prefecture, sent out scouts in separate parties, put battle and defense equipment in order, fought a great battle at Xieling Bridge, and the people of Guang were then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Braving snow he traveled by night and raced to the prefecture by forced marches. He sent out scouts, put battle equipment in order, fought a great battle at Xieling Bridge, and the people of Guangzhou were secured.

sentences.zh: 督府魏了翁以書來慰安之，以緡錢十萬勞其軍。

translations.literal: Supervisor Wei Liaoweng sent a letter to comfort him and gave one hundred thousand strings to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Wei Liaoweng sent a letter of comfort and gave one hundred thousand strings to reward his army.

sentences.zh: 霆以召，尋為吉州刺史，仍知光州。

translations.literal: Ting was summoned; soon he was made prefect of Jizhou while still governing Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was summoned to court and soon appointed prefect of Jizhou while still governing Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 霆固辭，丞相鄭清之、製置使史嵩之皆數以書留霆，霆不從，且曰：“士大夫當以世從道，不可以道從世也。”

translations.literal: Ting firmly declined; Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Shi Songzhi both repeatedly wrote by letter to detain Ting; Ting did not follow and added: "Scholar-officials should let the age follow the Way, not let the Way follow the age."
translations.idiomatic: Ting firmly declined. Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Shi Songzhi both wrote repeatedly urging him to stay. Ting refused and said, "Scholar-officials should let the age follow the Way, not let the Way follow the age."

sentences.zh: 再授閣門舍人，尋為達州刺史、右屯衛大將軍兼知蘄州，不赴。

translations.literal: He was again granted Gate Guard Attendant; soon made prefect of Dazhou and General of the Right Encampment Guard while also governing Qizhou; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Gate Guard Attendant, then prefect of Dazhou and General of the Right Encampment Guard while also governing Qizhou. He did not take up the posts.

sentences.zh: 尋遷淮西馬步軍副總管兼淮西遊擊軍副都統製。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Overall Commander of Huai West horse and foot armies while also Vice Commander-in-Chief of Huai West mobile armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Overall Commander of Huai West horse and foot armies and Vice Commander-in-Chief of Huai West mobile armies.

sentences.zh: 論遊擊軍十事，不報。

translations.literal: He discussed ten matters concerning mobile armies; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten proposals concerning the mobile armies. No response was given.

sentences.zh: 提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was made intendant of Chongxi Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of Chongxi Observatory.

sentences.zh: 知高郵軍，流民邦傑聚眾三千人為盜，霆剿其渠魁，餘黨悉散。

translations.literal: As prefect of Gaoyou Command, displaced person Bang Jie gathered a crowd of three thousand as bandits; Ting suppressed their ringleaders and the rest all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Gaoyou Command, a refugee named Bang Jie gathered three thousand men as bandits. Ting destroyed their ringleaders and the rest dispersed.

sentences.zh: 時議出師，和者甚多，霆以為：“莫若遣間探覘敵情，如不得已然後行之；

translations.literal: At the time expedition was discussed; many favored peace; Ting considered: "Better to send scouts to observe enemy conditions; if there is no other way, then act;"
translations.idiomatic: At the time an expedition was debated and many favored peace. Ting argued: "Better to send scouts to observe the enemy. Only if there is no other way should we act;"

sentences.zh: 否則無故自蕩其根本，是外兵未至而內兵先慘烈也。”

translations.literal: "otherwise without cause one shakes one's own foundation—this is outer troops not yet arrived while inner troops first suffer cruelly."
translations.idiomatic: "otherwise we will needlessly shake our own foundations—the outer enemy has not yet arrived while our own forces will suffer first."

sentences.zh: 諸軍畢行，惟高郵遲之，境內賴以安全。

translations.literal: All armies fully marched; only Gaoyou delayed; within the borders they relied on this for security.
translations.idiomatic: All armies marched out, but Gaoyou delayed, and the region relied on this for its security.

sentences.zh: 由是與時迕，而讒者益眾。

translations.literal: From this he went against the times, and slanderers grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From this he fell out with prevailing opinion, and his slanderers grew more numerous.

sentences.zh: 提舉雲台觀。

translations.literal: He was made intendant of Yuntai Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of Yuntai Observatory.

sentences.zh: 執政期論邊事，且謂朝廷即有齊安之命。

translations.literal: Those in power scheduled discussion of frontier affairs and added the court would soon have the Qi'an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power scheduled a discussion of frontier affairs and said the court would soon appoint him to Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 霆曰：“秋防已急，邊守不宜臨時更易，盍少需之。”

translations.literal: Ting said: "Autumn defense is already urgent; frontier defenders should not be changed at the last moment—why not wait a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "Autumn defense is already urgent. Frontier commanders should not be changed at the last moment. Why not wait a little?"

sentences.zh: 乃授帶行左領軍衛大將軍，充沿江製置副使司計議官，霆乃撰《沿江等邊志》一編上之。

translations.literal: He was then granted Acting General of the Left Leading Army Guard, serving as planning officer for the Vice Pacification Commission along the river; Ting then compiled one fascicle of Record of Frontier Regions along the River and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted Acting General of the Left Leading Army Guard and appointed planning officer for the Vice Pacification Commission along the Yangzi. Ting compiled Record of Frontier Regions along the River and presented it to court.

sentences.zh: 製置使董槐、鄧泳交薦之，差知壽昌軍，改蘄州，建學舍，祠忠臣。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioners Dong Huai and Deng Yong repeatedly recommended him; he was assigned to Shouchang Command, changed to Qizhou, built school quarters, and set up shrines to loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioners Dong Huai and Deng Yong repeatedly recommended him. He was assigned to Shouchang Command, then transferred to Qizhou, where he built school quarters and erected shrines to loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 嚐歎曰：“兩淮藩籬也，大江門戶也，三輔堂奧也。

translations.literal: He once sighed and said: "The Two Huai are the fence; the Great River is the gate; the Three Assistants are the inner hall."
translations.idiomatic: He once sighed and said, "The Two Huai are the fence, the Great River is the gate, and the capital region is the inner hall."

sentences.zh: 藩籬不固則門戶且危，門戶既危則堂奧豈能久安乎？”

translations.literal: If the fence is not solid then the gate is in peril; if the gate is already in peril how can the inner hall long be secure?
translations.idiomatic: If the fence is not secure, the gate is in peril. If the gate is in peril, how can the inner hall long remain secure?

sentences.zh: 於是貽書丞相杜範，乞瞰江審察形勢，置三新城：蘄春置於龍眼磯，安慶置於孟城，滁陽置於宣化。

translations.literal: He therefore sent a letter to Chief Councilor Du Fan, asking to overlook the river and examine terrain, establishing three new cities: Qichun at Longyan Rock, Anqing at Mengcheng, Chuyang at Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote to Chief Councilor Du Fan, asking to survey the Yangzi and assess the terrain, and proposed three new fortresses: Qichun at Longyan Rock, Anqing at Mengcheng, and Chuyang at Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 初，其父析業，霆獨以讓其兄。

translations.literal: Earlier, when his father divided the estate, Ting alone yielded his share to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When his father divided the family estate, Ting alone yielded his share to his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 處宗族有恩意，嚐訓其子弟曰：“窮理盡性，學之本也。”

translations.literal: In dealing with the clan he had gracious intent; he once instructed his sons and younger kin: "Exhausting principle and fulfilling nature is the root of learning."
translations.idiomatic: He treated his clan with kindness and once instructed his sons and younger kin: "Exhausting principle and fulfilling nature is the root of learning."

sentences.zh: 有《玉溪集》行於世。

translations.literal: He had Jade Stream Collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Jade Stream Collection circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：吳昌裔訪道東南，一何勤哉！

translations.literal: The discussion says: Wu Changyi sought the Way in the southeast—how diligent!
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Wu Changyi sought the Way in the southeast—how diligent he was!

sentences.zh: 故其造深醇，見諸事功者，足以知其學無雜也。

translations.literal: Therefore his achievement was deep and pure; what appears in practical accomplishments suffices to know his learning had no admixture.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement was deep and pure, and what appears in his practical accomplishments shows that his learning had no admixture.

sentences.zh: 汪綱之遺愛在越，先民所謂擇賢久任者，固不我欺矣。

translations.literal: Wang Gang's lingering love was in Yue; what the ancients called choosing the worthy and employing them long—truly they did not deceive us.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gang's enduring benevolence in Yue shows that the ancients were right when they said to choose the worthy and employ them long.

sentences.zh: 陳宓以宰相子，論諫之直，於今有光。

translations.literal: Chen Mi as a chief councilor's son—his directness in remonstrance and discussion still shines today.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mi, though a chief councilor's son, shone with the directness of his remonstrance, and that light endures today.

sentences.zh: 王霆通兵家言，而謂不可以道從世，此古人謀帥貴乎“說《禮》、《樂》而敦《詩》、《書》”也。

translations.literal: Wang Ting was versed in military theorists' words yet said one cannot let the Way follow the age—this is what the ancients meant in seeking commanders when they valued "expounding Rites and Music and honoring Odes and Documents."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ting was versed in military theory yet held that one cannot let the Way follow the age. This is what the ancients meant when they sought commanders who "expound the Rites and Music and honor the Odes and Documents."
